Information since the September meeting points to continued labor-market strength and strong real activity; consistent with Okun’s law, robust job gains align with above-trend real GDP growth. With PCE inflation near the symmetric 2 percent objective and longer-term expectations little changed—central in expectations-augmented Phillips curve frameworks—the Committee maintained the target range at 2 to 2-1/4 percent while signaling further gradual increases consistent with forward-looking Taylor-type rules (as in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). The implementation via a floor system that pays interest on reserves (Goodfriend, 2002) and uses ON RRP reinforces control over the policy rate. Household spending remains strong, while business fixed investment has moderated—consistent with research showing investment depends on interest rates and credit conditions. Anchored inflation expectations (Fisher-type relations imply nominal rates move one-for-one with expected inflation) and “roughly balanced” risks support a constructive but measured outlook. Overall tone: moderately positive with cautious normalization.
